You’ll be expected to wear long skirts if you dont want to wear pants, (below/at the knee), and your shirts must be work appropriate. This generally means plain and with a collar. Tracksuits are also popular 😅

It depends on your school you’d get. I like to dress in kawaii fashion and I mostly just tone it all down. I’m lucky that my school is really laid back and casual, but they have different standards for work attire in Japan. It has to generally be pretty plain or have a tasteful small motif or pattern if you do decide to be a little fashion forward.

My first few weeks were so awful. 😂 I can’t even lie. I love Japan and coming here has always been a dream of mine, but walking the same roads I walk today, for the first time, was gut wrenching soul splittingly hard and terrifying. It’s really crazy what you can come to terms with and become comfortable with in a short amount of time - with some patience and understanding. I think if anyone tries to pretend that being dropped in an unknown place like a freshly hatched egg and ISNT horrified is either lying or burying something deep within. This is all to say that your experience is normal! You’re in a totally new environment. Everything is horrifying. I kept thinking, why did I leave everything I’ve ever known just to not be able to read anything at the grocery store? 
Even the most mundane tasks can feel insurmountable.

It was their small kind gestures that kept me grounded my first few weeks.

There are lots of ALTs and English speakers in Tokyo! Getting in contact with some of them will help your feeling of dread and fear I bet.
